html:
Violeta Barrios de Chamorro was the president of Nicaragua from 1990 to 1997, the first woman elected head of state in the Americas. She defeated the Sandinistas in the election of 1990.

She was the widow of Pedro Joaquín Chamorro, the newspaper editor whose murder in 1978 set off the revolution. She served briefly in the first revolutionary junta, then broke with the Sandinistas and ran their newspaper, La Prensa, against them. In 1990 a broad alliance chose her to run against Daniel Ortega, and she won a clear victory.

She ended the war with the Contras, cut the army and ended the draft, and brought down huge inflation. Her government kept the peace between enemies in Nicaragua. She died in exile in Costa Rica in 2025.
